verbs.name: screen_record.status
verbs.description: Read the short-lived first-screen-frame admission fact for one active capture in this cutd process. This is not crash recovery, output validation, a timer, or a process-start acknowledgement: ready becomes true only after the active native screen path delivered a real screen frame (Windows: accepted by the MP4 encoder; macOS: ScreenCaptureKit screen-sample callback; Linux: PipeWire screen buffer delivered through the GStreamer observer). It never opens a device, starts/stops a capture, reads a media file, exposes a path, or persists a fact. Terminal states are deliberately not ready even if a frame arrived earlier. A completed capture or server restart returns not_found rather than inferring readiness from artifacts.

capture_id.description: The exact active capture id returned by screen_record.start. It is an opaque identifier, never a path.

verbs.result: {capture_id, ready, terminal, state:"awaiting_first_screen_frame"|"ready"|"terminal_before_first_screen_frame"|"terminal_after_first_screen_frame"} — proceed only when ready:true and terminal:false. ready is false until the actual native screen-frame delivery boundary, and becomes false permanently when the active capture terminalizes; terminal_after_first_screen_frame retains only the diagnostic ordering, not an admission to stop/continue. not_found means that no matching capture is active in this cutd process.
